clue.text: Novel photo wife put in boot with ID

parts.note: pic is a casual word for a photo

indicators.note: the wife's letter is set inside the word for boot

parts.note: to boot is to kick
identity documents are your papers

explanation.surface: A detective note: a picture of a wife stuffed into a car boot along with her identity card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boot' looks like the car's luggage space, but it is the verb, giving KICK; W goes after its first K.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's first novel, The Pickwick Papers, is the book meant here.

clue.text: In the past a massive herbivore, one dropping kebab without hesitation

definitions.text: In the past a massive herbivore

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
guano is bird droppings

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is taken away from the kebab word

parts.note: a doner is a kind of kebab
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A huge plant-eater from long ago is pictured dropping its kebab with no hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: DONER loses ER to leave DON.
explanation.definitionFit: This dinosaur was a large plant-eater that lived millions of years ago, so it fits a massive herbivore of the past.

clue.text: What worshipper might do to raise shelter needed by Kingston's outsiders

indicators.note: the outside letters of the place name Kingston are taken
in a down clue raising a word turns it to read upwards

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A worshipper in Kingston needs to put up a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' suits a down clue, where the word reads upwards; 'outsiders' are the first and last letters of Kingston.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on bended knees is the posture of someone at prayer in church.

clue.text: Writer's vivacity, when keeping log, stirred confusing situation

parts.note: the writer is the setter, so writer's is I'm, contracted to IM

indicators.note: the lively word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: brio is liveliness or vivacity

indicators.note: stirring mixes up the letters of log

explanation.surface: An author's lively style, when keeping a diary, stirred up a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' is the setter speaking, I'm; 'stirred' scrambles log to GLO before 'keeping' holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a tangled, embarrassing state of affairs, a muddled predicament.

clue.text: Tart dressing up to exit sailing boat

indicators.note: the word up leaves the sauce

parts.note: a sharp, tangy sauce for food is ketchup
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman gets dressed up to leave a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' is the adjective sharp, not a pastry or a woman; KETCHUP loses UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Sort of hide everybody on vacation in Genoa during violent riot

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: the city's outer letters come in the middle of the jumbled riot
violent signals the letters of riot thrown about
Genoa emptied of its inner letters leaves just its outsides

explanation.surface: Everyone on holiday in the Italian port gets caught up in a violent riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' scrambles riot to ITOR; 'on vacation' empties Genoa of its middle, and 'during' puts what is left after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin of this reptile is tanned as a leather, a type of hide used for bags and shoes.

clue.text: Muse, time and time again, on Oscar

parts.note: an era is a period of time
T is the abbreviation for time, the second time it is used
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone thinks, time after time, about the Oscars.
explanation.definitionFit: She is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Woman forecasting weather's latest feature in six directions

indicators.note: the last letter appears in the middle of the compass letters

parts.note: six compass points, S, E, E, E, S and S

indicators.note: the latest letter of weather is its final one

explanation.surface: A female forecaster says the weather will come in from every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points such as S and E are crossword shorthand for directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A seeress is a female prophet who foretells the future.

clue.text: Pungent plant reflected sunlight on bank

indicators.note: a reflection shows the word backwards, so the sunbeam is read in reverse

parts.note: a ray is a beam of sunlight
a bank of seats or keys is a row

explanation.surface: A strong-smelling plant catches sunlight on a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a strongly scented flowering herb of the daisy family.

clue.text: Blue streetmap certain to lose its front

parts.note: an A to Z is a British book of street maps, written A-Z

indicators.note: the word for certain drops its first letter

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Someone feeling down about the street atlas is sure to lose its cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-Z is a well-known London street atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is the clear bright blue of a cloudless sky.

clue.text: Overbearing woman from Hastings perhaps cross in casualty

parts.note: the Battle of Hastings, 1066, is an example of a battle

indicators.note: the cross is put inside the hospital abbreviation

parts.note: A&E (accident and emergency) is the British hospital casualty department
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A domineering woman from the seaside town of Hastings gets angry in a hospital casualty ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Hastings looks like a place of origin, but it stands for the battle; A&E is Britain's hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleaxe is an informal term for a formidable, domineering older woman.

clue.text: European footballer cultivated land wearing jumper

indicators.note: the jumper has the other letters inside it, as though worn

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: land that is cultivated is worked over, so its letters are turned about

explanation.surface: A footballer from Europe has worked the land while wearing a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater but is the leaping kangaroo, ROO, which holds NALD from 'cultivated' land.
explanation.definitionFit: Cristiano Ronaldo is a famous Portuguese footballer, so a European player.

clue.text: House guest initially recognises reported snake

indicators.note: the first letter of guest is taken
reported means the word is as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to recognise someone is to know them, so recognises is knows

explanation.surface: A guest at a house is said to recognise a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOWS and NOSE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The hognose is a North American snake with an upturned snout.

clue.text: Joined, say, revolutionary club

parts.note: to wed is to join in marriage, so joined is wed

indicators.note: a revolution turns around, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Someone joined a revolutionary club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks political but reverses EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a type of golf club used for short, lofted shots.

clue.text: One determines the worth of foremost of artists in Louvre at broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered
the foremost letter of artists is taken

explanation.surface: A valuer examines art at the Louvre on a broadcast programme.
explanation.walkthrough: A from artists plus LOUVRE and AT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluator is someone who assesses value, judging how much a thing is worth.

clue.text: Religious text Clive reviewed, circulating it with American

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the jumbled letters surround it
reviewed suggests Clive's letters looked over again and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Clive reviews a religious text, passing it round with an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' scrambles the name to LEVIC, which 'circulating' wraps around the word it.
explanation.definitionFit: Leviticus is the third book of the Old Testament, a scriptural book.

clue.text: Victor has fever, head being hazy

definitions.note: a noun phrase meaning the state of lacking clarity

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ague is an old word for a malarial fever
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A man called Victor has a fever, his head foggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not the body part but a headland; NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being hazy is a lack of clarity, which is vagueness.

clue.text: US agents consuming beer and sport north of the border once

indicators.note: the agency's letters swallow the beer and sport words

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency
ale is a beer
to sport clothing is to don it, to wear it

explanation.surface: American agents drink beer and play sport in Scotland in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' is not a game but the verb, to wear proudly. North of the border is Scotland, seen from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the old Latin name for Scotland, the land north of the English border.

clue.text: Make mistake with lass performing good chant

parts.note: to sin is to go wrong
a gal is a girl or lass
a performer is on stage, on

explanation.surface: Someone errs with a girl performing a fine chant.
explanation.definitionFit: A singalong is a session of group singing, much like a chant everyone joins.

clue.text: Storage device is erected by Mike and Jack perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, erecting the word puts it upright so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the jack is a playing card

explanation.surface: A storage device is set up by two men, Mike and Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike and Jack look like names; Mike is M, and the jack is an example of a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A SIM card is a small chip that stores a phone subscriber's data.

clue.text: Centre of party hat, when turned round, illuminated again

indicators.note: the centre letter of party is taken
the hat word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A party hat, once turned round, is lit up again.
explanation.walkthrough: Tile is old slang for a hat; 'when turned round' makes it ELIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lit once more, like a relit candle, has been illuminated again.

clue.text: Excellent advice by spinner

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: Great advice from a spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler who spins the ball; here it is a spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal word for first-rate or excellent.

clue.text: Shakespearean character having coat of poor quality

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat
duff is British slang for useless or of poor quality

explanation.surface: A stage actor in a Shakespeare play is wearing a shoddy costume coat.
explanation.walkthrough: DUFF is everyday British slang for worthless or broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Macduff is the Thane of Fife who slays Macbeth in the Scottish play.

clue.text: Clobber son required: black suit

parts.note: to clobber is to hit hard, to club

explanation.surface: Someone's clobber, their gear, needs a son to wear a black suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes, fitting 'suit', but here it is the verb, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is one of the two black suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Scotsman leaves dairy cattle food for grazing?

indicators.note: the Scotsman goes away from the cattle breed

parts.note: Friesians are a black-and-white breed of dairy cow
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman leaves his dairy cows food to graze on.
explanation.walkthrough: Grazing here is snacking, nibbling through the day, not cattle eating grass; FRIESIAN minus IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips are a snack people pick at, and grazing is slang for constant nibbling.

clue.text: Arrived eventually, then Jade only half-finished flipping dessert

indicators.note: only the back half of each of the two words is kept, the rest finished off
flipping turns the pudding word over to read backwards

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: Someone got there in the end, then Jade only half finished her dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half-finished' leaves the back halves of 'then' and 'Jade', EN and DE; 'flipping' turns PUD into DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is to reach it finally, often after a roundabout route.

clue.text: First attempt mostly good? Correct

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its final letter cut

parts.note: a debut is a first appearance or attempt

explanation.surface: Was a first attempt mostly good? Yes, correct.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBUT loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: To debug code is to find and correct its errors.

clue.text: Stop among motoring group in English region of France

indicators.note: the stop word goes between the letters of the motoring group

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation
to quit is to stop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A motoring group stops in an English part of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the British breakdown and motoring association; 'English' looks like it qualifies the region but gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquitaine is a historic region in south-west France, once ruled by English kings.

clue.text: Five characters in Cuban joint strumming instrument

indicators.note: five consecutive letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A strummed instrument is played in a Cuban bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in cuBAN JOint.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument played by strumming or plucking.

clue.text: Woman's hair and nails restyled around end of spring. Mayday?

parts.note: Di is a woman's name, so woman's is DI'S
a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the final letter
restyling the nails reshapes their letters
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of spring is used

explanation.surface: A woman restyles her hair and nails at the end of spring, perhaps on May Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restyled' turns NAILS into SINAL, which goes 'around' G, the end of spring. May Day, 1 May, suggests the spring date.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayday is the international radio call made by a ship or aircraft in serious trouble.
